preamble: Denasalization of [ĩ] to oral [i]. In Middle French, vowels that had been nasalized before a nasal consonant lost their nasality when that consonant remained before a vowel, so Old French fine [ˈfĩnə] became [fin] and ligne [ˈlĩɲə] became [liɲ], while in closed syllables the nasal vowel survived and lowered (fin [fɛ̃]).

examples.note: Middle French denasalization before /n/ or /m/ followed by a vowel; the masculine fin, where the nasal closed the syllable, kept and lowered the nasal vowel as [fɛ̃].
The same denasalization before an intervocalic palatal nasal /ɲ/.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Phonological history of French. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phonological_history_of_French
